subject: French
examFormat: Three papers, all to be taken; Papers 1 and 2 form a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: 40 multiple-choice questions in 1 hour for 40 marks (Section A Comprehension: two passages of about 150 words with five questions each; Section B Structure: thirty short questions). Paper 2: essay and letter writing, three questions in each section, one answered from each (about 100 words each), 1 hour 15 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 3: listening comprehension, reading aloud and conversation, 40 minutes per candidate for 50 marks.
excluded: Suggested reading lists, grammar books, dictionaries and the Literature set texts (marked Ghana only). The remark that five of the dialogue questions in the conversation test are on literature texts applies to Ghana only.

topics.name: Comprehension (Paper 1, Section A)
objectives: Read and understand standard written documents in French
topics.content: Two passages, each of about 150 words, with a total of five short multiple-choice questions on each. Candidates answer all questions.

topics.name: Structure (Paper 1, Section B)
objectives: Use French words, expressions and structural patterns in appropriate communicative contexts
topics.content: Thirty short questions; candidates attempt all of them. Structure is tested, as far as possible, within suitable communicative contexts.

topics.name: Essay (Paper 2, Section A)
objectives: Write freely and correctly on topics of general interest using appropriate structures, registers and tenses
topics.content: Three questions are set and candidates answer one, in about 100 words.

topics.name: Letter Writing (Paper 2, Section B)
objectives: Write formal and informal letters using appropriate structures, registers and tenses
topics.content: Three questions are set and candidates answer one, in about 100 words.

topics.name: Listening Comprehension (Paper 3)
objectives: Listen to and understand a straightforward passage in French
Answer questions on the passage in writing
topics.content: A passage of about 200 words on issues of general interest is read aloud by the examiner. In the first 10 minutes it is read twice; candidates study the questions for 3 minutes before the second reading and have 7 minutes after it to answer 10 questions in writing. Questions may include open-ended questions, transformation and substitution as well as multiple choice.

topics.name: Reading Aloud (Paper 3)
objectives: Read aloud with appropriate pronunciation and fluency
topics.content: A simple passage of about 100 words of contemporary interest is read once at a normal pace.

topics.name: Conversation (Paper 3)
objectives: Express oneself freely in a dialogue, responding to a minimum of ten questions
Speak freely on a given topic in French, making a minimum of five sentences
topics.content: The conversation lasts about 10 minutes per candidate. Topics are drawn from general and contemporary themes such as sports, health, leisure, education, politics and culture. There are two parts: dialogue and exposition.

topics.name: Notes on Structure: Grammar and Usage
objectives: Use the parts of speech (grammatical categories)
Use definite, indefinite and partitive articles (gender and number where applicable)
Use regular and irregular verbs in the common moods and tenses
Use standard expressions such as avoir + noun (e.g. avoir faim) and venir de + infinitive
Use nouns and their complements, gender and number
Use personal, possessive, indefinite, demonstrative, relative and impersonal pronouns
Use possessive, demonstrative, indefinite and interrogative adjectives (agreement and position)
Form and place adverbs, including special adverbs such as mal, vite, fort, tout
Use negative expressions (ne...pas, ne...rien, ne...jamais, etc.)
Use common conjunctions: et, mais, donc, ou, parce que, etc.
Use prepositions: à, de, sur, en, devant, etc.
Use declarative, interrogative and exclamative sentence patterns
Use the active and passive voice
Use direct and reported speech
Use compound and complex sentences
Use idiomatic expressions and proverbs
Use formal and informal forms of writing
Convey context and meaning, e.g. politeness, disgust, disappointment
Use common figures of speech (similes, metaphors, hyperbole)
Use the structures of major actes de parole (exprimer la déception, la probation, le dégoût, la surprise, le plaisir, le regret, etc.)
